# Autoslide Programmers Guide

Note: All information in this guide was gathered via reverse engineering. Commands and responses were observed on the serial lines when the OEM BLE microcontroller device was installed and communicating with the autoslide door. There may be small errors or assumptions about the capabilities or operational flow of the door. When in doubt, be conservative about the implementation.

## Summary

The autoslide automatic door opener can be attached to a standard sliding door to give it electric assist and automatic opening capabilities. It includes a serial interface allowing users to control it with their own devices. The following is an implementation guide for the programming interface

## Connections

There is a 4 pin connector on the board labeled “Wifi” that includes 12V power, ground, and a 5V UART interface. The UART interface operates at 19200 baud. 

Connections to the wifi module are shown below, when viewing the front side of the PCB with all LED’s, power connectors on the left side, and input triggers on the right.   
 

| Door Rx (5V signal) |
| :---- |
| Door Tx (5V signal) |
| Door 12V |
| Door Gnd |

      ![][image1]  
Note: The UART connection is shared with the OEM BLE microcontroller module that exists on the back side of the PCB. For best results, it is recommended to disconnect the BLE microcontroller before attempting to connect to communicate with the module. It does seem possible to exist in tandem with the module, but could result in undefined behavior.

## Basic Protocol

All commands sent to the door device follow the **AT command** structure. An AT command consists of a prefix **AT+**, then the command type, then a payload of comma separated list of key value pairs, then an **escape character** (0x1B, `^[` or `\e`). Any command between the Autoslide and the commanding device will begin with “AT+” and be terminated with “\\e”. The key value pairs will consist of a single letter, a colon, and then numbers. Example complete commands that can be received over the wire:

* AT+UPDATE,a:0\\e  
  * AT+UPDATE,b:0\\e  
    * AT+UPSEND,m:2,c:1,n:0\\e  
    * AT+REPLY,r:1\\e  
    * AT+RESULT,r:1\\e

The controlling device can send **AT+UPDATE** commands to control the Autoslide. The Autoslide should always reply to these update commands with an **AT+RESULT,r:1\\e**. The result can contain the payload **r:1** to indicate success, or it can contain other key value pairs as a response to the update request. If the reply contains other data besides **r:1**, this is considered a success. The **AT+UPDATE** command can send any command to change the state of the Autoslide. Only a single key/value pair should be sent to the autoslide. No additional commands should be sent to the door until the successful result has been received. A 1 second timeout can be used if no result is received

The Autoslide can send data to the controlling device at any time using the **AT+UPSEND** command. The upsend command will contain information from the Autoslide about current state or settings. The door expects to receive an **AT+REPLY,r:1** response to indicate it has been received. No other commands should be sent to the device until the reply has been sent. The upsend can be but is not always triggered by a request from the controlling device.

## Startup

On startup, the opener will perform a routine where it cycles the door to ensure travel extents. Once the door has closed during this sweep, it will upsend information to indicate that it has finished closing. Sending commands to the opener before this initial sweep can result in undefined behavior. Immediately sending data on powerup seems to result in the opener’s Rx line being disabled. Observations have shown that the initial startup routine should take less than 25 seconds

## Feedback

The Autoslide has hardware methods of triggering the door to open and change modes. If the user changes door modes or triggers a door open using these hardware methods, the door will perform some action and send an upsend command with an update of its current state. When the user triggers the door to open manually, either with the button, pet collar trigger, or by pulling on the door, the door will start moving and upsend the current motion state, lock state, and motion trigger. When the user toggles the door mode, it will first upsend its new door mode, then it will immediately close/open or lock/unlock the door depending on the state transition. It will then send the motion state, lock state, and motion trigger again since it has effectively changed motion states.

## Payload Keys

The following table explains all of the possible keys, their meaning, if they are writable, and their valid range.

| Name | Key | Writeable | Type | Valid Range | Description or Enum Values |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| door mode | a | yes | enum | 0-3 | 0:MODE\_AUTO 1:MODE\_STACK 2:MODE\_LOCK 3:MODE\_PET |
| open speed | e | yes | enum | 0-1 | 0:OPEN\_SPEED\_FAST 1:OPEN\_SPEED\_SLOW |
| secure pet | g | yes | enum | 0-1 | 0: SECURE\_PET\_ON 1:SECURE\_PET\_OFF |
| open hold duration | j | yes | integer | 0-25 | Seconds. MUST BE 2 DIGITS |
| open force | C | yes | integer | 0-7 | force value |
| close force | z | yes | integer | 0-7 | force value |
| close end force | A | yes | integer | 0-7 | force value |
| trigger open | b | yes | integer | 1-3 | 1:TRIGGER\_INDOOR 2:TRIGGER\_PET 3:TRIGGER\_STACK |
| status request | d | yes | enum | 0-1 | 0:REQUEST\_ALL\_SETTINGS 1:REQUEST\_VERSION\_INFO |
| motion state | m | no | enum | 0-2 | 0:MOTION\_STOPPED 1:MOTION\_OPENING 2:MOTION\_CLOSING |
| locked | c | no | enum | 0-1 | 0:UNLOCKED 1:LOCKED |
| motion trigger | n | no | enum | 0-5 | 0:MOTION\_TRIGGER\_NONE 1:MOTION\_TRIGGER\_INDOOR 2:MOTION\_TRIGGER\_MASTER 3:MOTION\_TRIGGER\_PET 4:MOTION\_TRIGGER\_STACK 5:MOTION\_TRIGGER\_SOFTWARE |

## Examples

* Request door open with TRIGGER\_MASTER  
  * Controlling device sends “AT+UPDATE,b:0\\e” to the door  
  * Autoslide responds with “AT+RESULT,r:1\\e”   
    * r:1 indicates command was received and performed successfully  
    * r:0 indicates command was not performed successfully  
    * The door is ready to receive another command after it sends the RESULT command  
* Request door mode MODE\_LOCK  
  * Controlling device sends “AT+UPDATE,b:0\\e” to the door  
  * Autoslide responds with “AT+RESULT,r:1\\e”   
    * r:1 indicates command was received and performed successfully  
    * r:0 indicates command was not performed successfully  
    * The door is ready to receive another command after it sends the RESULT command  
* Request open hold duration of 15 seconds  
  * Controlling device sends “AT+UPDATE,j:15\\e” to the door  
  * Autoslide responds with “AT+RESULT,r:1\\e”   
    * r:1 indicates command was received and performed successfully  
    * r:0 indicates command was not performed successfully  
    * The door is ready to receive another command after it sends the RESULT command  
* Request Current Settings  
  * Controlling device sends “AT+UPDATE,d:0\\e” to the door  
  * Autoslide responds with “AT+RESULT,a:0,e:1,g:0,C:0,j:01,z:0,A:7\\e”  
    * “a” is the key for current mode  
    * “e” is the key for open speed  
    * “g” is the key for secure pet mode  
    * “C” is the key for open force  
    * “j” is the key for open duration  
    * “z” is the key for close force  
    * “A” is the key for close end force  
* Autoslide sends its current state periodically  
  * Unprompted, the Autoslide sends “AT+UPSEND,m:2,c:1,n:0\\e”  
    * “m” is the key for motion state  
    * “c” is the key for lock state  
    * “n” is the key for motion trigger  
  * Controlling device must respond “AT+REPLY,r:1” to indicate the request has been received  
    * Autoslide will not respond to new commands until it receives the response
